title: How To Use A Vape Pen For Weed
summary: We sell weed on the internet. Thousands of products delivered overnight throughout California from Humboldt to San Diego
body_text: Pocket-sized, discreet, and easy to use, vape pens are all the rage in weed consumption. Once used primarily for nicotine vaping, these versatile devices are a simple and portable way to enjoy cannabis flower, distillates, oil, and vape juice. Vaping offers a healthier alternative to smoking weed since there is little-to-no combustion involved; combustion is the primary cause of carcinogen release in traditional weed consumption. (It's important to note different vapes produce varying amounts of benzopyrene, the primary carcinogen released when burning organic materials. The amount released is dependent on the design of the cape and the vaporization process.) Instead, vape pens transform liquids, concentrates, or flower, into vapor via a vape tank or cartridge, giving you more control over the strength of your dose on the inhale. If you're new to vaping, you'll need some basic pointers to get started. Read on for our ultimate guide on how to use a vape pen. What is a Vape Pen? A vape pen, sometimes called a hash oil pen, is a portable pen-shaped device that heats cannabis concentrates in a small internal chamber or cartridge to a temperature at which the active compounds transform into vapor without combustion. Smaller than tabletop and portable vaporizers, vape pens are either rechargeable or disposable. A rechargeable vape pen has a chargeable battery and can be fitted with various interchangeable chambers and atomizers. A disposable vape pen has a one-and-done design with an internal battery, prefilled cartridge, and coil atomizer and is meant to be disposed of once depleted. Both rechargeable and disposable pens come in two main types: push-button and draw-activated. Push-button vape pens must be turned on via the power button, which also controls the heat setting. Draw-activated vape pens are turned on by merely puffing on them, making them the simplest to use but with less control over options like temperature than push-button devices. How Do Vape Pens Work? To understand how to use a vape pen, it's helpful to know the basics of how a vape pen works. Both disposable and rechargeable vape pens are made up of the same essential parts: 1. Mouthpiece: As the name implies, this is where you draw the vapor. The mouthpiece attaches to the top of the pen above the heating chamber. 2. The heating chamber or cartridge and atomizer: This is where concentrates like cannabis oil or wax are loaded and heated by a battery-powered element until they produce vapor. 3. Battery: Attached to the cartridge and atomizer, the battery is the longest part of the pen and is the power source for heating the cartridge. 4. Charger: Rechargeable models include a USB charger and cable to juice up the vape pen battery. A vape pen works by heating the substance in the chamber or cartridge via the battery-powered coil to just below the point of combustion (356° to 374°F) to activate the cannabis compound's vapor form. This vapor is inhaled through the mouthpiece. How To Vape Weed: A Step-by-Step Guide Can you vape weed? Yes! Vaping weed is both a healthier and more discreet alternative than smoking. Instead of smoke, vape pens produce a virtually odorless vapor free of tar and many carcinogens. Here's a step-by-step guide covering how to use a vape pen for weed: 1. Check the battery. Make sure that the battery is charged on a rechargeable pen before assembly. 2. Assemble the pen. Disposable pens are preloaded and ready to go. If you are using a rechargeable pen, assemble the correct order pieces, including the heating chamber. You can load the chamber yourself with the concentrate of your choice or opt for a pre-filled oil cartridge. Once you've assembled the pen, wait a few moments for the oil to penetrate the heating coil. 3. Turn on the pen. Disposable vape pens are usually draw-activated, so simply inhale from the mouthpiece to turn on. A push-button vape pen must be turned on by clicking the power button five times in a row and waiting for the light to turn on, indicating that the pen is ready. Inhale from the mouthpiece while pressing and holding the power button down. 4. Adjust the heat. Many rechargeable pens allow you to adjust the heat by pushing the power button three times. 5. Turn the power off. When you are finished, push the power button five times to turn the power off of rechargeable pens. Disposable pens can simply be discarded when depleted. Vape Pens vs. Dab Pens Standard vape pens work with cartridges designed for cannabis oil or distillate. In contrast, dab pens—also known as wax pens—are compatible with many forms of concentrate in dab form, including wax, batter/badder, budder, and shatter. Dab pens are generally composed of the same essential parts as a vape pen and work the same way. Still, the heating chamber can be loaded with solid dabs, and the design allows for more airflow and higher temperatures required for vaporizing dabs (concentrated wax). Read on to learn more about how to hit a dab pen. How to Use a Dab Pen If you've ever used a vape pen, you'll find these instructions on how to use a wax pen or dab pen familiar. 1. Check the battery and recharge if needed. For information on how to charge a dab pen for your specific device, check the instruction manual. 2. Assemble the pen. Load a small amount of wax with a dab tool into the heating chamber without overloading it, or you can cause clogging or leaking. Ensure room for oxygen to flow. 3. Prime the coil. Gently pulse the fire button to begin melting the wax. 4. Inhale. Hold the button down, starting with small puffs. 5. Adjust the heat. Pulse the button while inhaling rather than holding it down if the chamber is getting too hot. We hope our overview of how to use a vape pen answered all your questions about this conveniently compact and odor-free device.

title: FIDO2 vs U2F 5 Key Differences Explained
summary: Understand the differences between FIDO2 and U2F. Learn how each works, where they apply, and which authentication standard to choose.
body_text: Authentication standards evolve to address real security gaps. Passwords can be stolen. OTPs can be intercepted. U2F (Universal 2nd Factor) arrived in 2014 to solve this problem using public-key cryptography and physical security keys. Users authenticate with a password plus a hardware token that attackers cannot replicate remotely. FIDO2 expanded this model in 2018 by introducing WebAuthn and CTAP2, enabling both multi-factor and fully passwordless authentication through security keys, fingerprint sensors, or facial recognition. Both standards bind credentials to specific origins, which blocks phishing, credential stuffing, and man-in-the-middle attacks. A fake login page at a different domain simply cannot request valid credentials. U2F established the foundation. FIDO2 builds on it with broader capabilities, but their long-term viability and supported use cases differ significantly. 1. Scope of Use U2F : operates exclusively as a second factor. Users must first authenticate with a password before U2F verification occurs. The security key proves possession of a registered device but cannot replace the initial authentication step. FIDO2 : supports both multi-factor and passwordless authentication. In multi-factor mode, it functions similarly to U2F. In passwordless mode, the security key becomes the sole authentication method. Users verify their identity through biometrics or a PIN on the authenticator itself, eliminating passwords entirely. Why This Matters : This architectural difference affects deployment strategy. Organizations using U2F must maintain password infrastructure: reset flows, complexity requirements, and rotation policies. With FIDO2 passwordless authentication, these concerns disappear. 2. Underlying Standards U2F : operates as a single specification published by the FIDO Alliance. The standard defines the complete authentication flow: browser communication, cryptographic operations, and data formats. This unified approach simplified initial adoption but limited flexibility. FIDO2 : splits functionality across two complementary standards. WebAuthn provides the browser API that web applications use to request authentication. CTAP2 (Client to Authenticator Protocol 2) defines how clients communicate with authenticators, whether external security keys or platform authenticators like Windows Hello or Touch ID. Why This Matters : This separation creates clear responsibility boundaries. WebAuthn standardizes what developers implement, regardless of which authenticator users choose. CTAP2 handles device communication, allowing authenticator manufacturers to innovate without breaking web applications. CTAP2 includes CTAP1, which provides U2F functionality, enabling backward compatibility during migration. 3. Device Compatibility U2F : authenticates exclusively through external hardware tokens. Users must purchase and carry physical security keys like YubiKey or Titan Security Key. The protocol has no mechanism for using biometrics or built-in device capabilities. FIDO2 : authenticates through both external keys and platform authenticators. Platform authenticators leverage hardware already present in devices: fingerprint sensors on laptops, facial recognition on smartphones, or TPM chips in computers. Windows Hello, Touch ID, Face ID, and Android biometric authentication all function as FIDO2 authenticators. Why This Matters : This flexibility changes deployment economics. Organizations can implement FIDO2 without purchasing additional hardware for users with compatible devices. A laptop with a fingerprint reader or a phone with Face ID becomes the authenticator. Platform authenticators improve user experience for single-device scenarios, but external keys provide portability across devices. 4. Browser & Platform Support U2F : reached peak browser support around 2017 before browsers began deprecating it. Chrome deprecated the U2F API in Chrome 98 (2022) and removed it entirely in Chrome 115 (2023). Firefox deprecated U2F in favor of WebAuthn starting in version 60. Safari never implemented U2F natively. FIDO2 : through WebAuthn has universal modern browser support. Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge all implement the WebAuthn standard with full functionality. Mobile browsers on iOS and Android support FIDO2, enabling authentication on smartphones and tablets. Why This Matters : Platform support extends to operating systems. Windows 10 and later include Windows Hello. macOS and iOS support Touch ID and Face ID through WebAuthn. Android devices use fingerprint sensors and facial recognition as platform authenticators. For new implementations, FIDO2 is the only viable choice. 5. Passwordless Capability U2F : cannot enable passwordless authentication. The protocol requires an initial password authentication before the second factor verification. This design limitation means U2F deployments must maintain complete password infrastructure, including reset mechanisms and complexity policies. FIDO2 : enables passwordless authentication through resident credentials (also called discoverable credentials or passkeys). The authenticator stores credential information locally, allowing users to authenticate without entering a username. The authentication flow becomes: connect authenticator, verify identity through biometrics or PIN, gain access. Why This Matters : Resident credentials work across devices when using external security keys. A YubiKey registered for passwordless authentication functions on any computer or mobile device that supports FIDO2. Platform authenticators create device-specific credentials: Touch ID credentials on a MacBook work only on that MacBook. The passwordless capability eliminates entire categories of password-related attacks: phishing, credential stuffing, password spraying, and database breaches. Organizations deploying FIDO2 passwordless authentication remove passwords from the attack surface for those users. Comparison Table Feature U2F FIDO2 Use Case 2FA only 2FA + Passwordless Standards U2F API WebAuthn + CTAP Devices Hardware keys Hardware + platform authenticators Browser Support Deprecated (removed from modern browsers) Universal (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge) Passwordless Support ❌ ✅ Which Should You Use Today? U2F : is a legacy standard. Chrome removed U2F API support in 2023, and other browsers either deprecated or never implemented it. Applications still using U2F APIs will break as browsers complete the removal process. FIDO2 : is the modern replacement, already powering passkeys and supported by tech giants (Apple, Google, Microsoft). New implementations should go directly to FIDO2 for future-proof authentication. Most security keys supporting U2F also support FIDO2, making hardware migration straightforward. Why This Matters : Organizations with existing U2F deployments should plan migration before browser support ends completely. The migration requires rewriting authentication code to use WebAuthn APIs, but this work becomes necessary regardless as browsers remove U2F support. How SuperTokens Fits Into FIDO2 Adoption Passwordless Support SuperTokens implements FIDO2 through the WebAuthn recipe, handling protocol complexity while exposing clean APIs for developers: import SuperTokens from "supertokens-node" ; import WebAuthn from "supertokens-node/recipe/webauthn" ; import Session from "supertokens-node/recipe/session" ; SuperTokens . init ( { appInfo : { appName : "Your App" , apiDomain : "https://api.example.com" , websiteDomain : "https://example.com" } , recipeList : [ WebAuthn . init ( ) , Session . init ( ) ] } ) ; The implementation supports both platform authenticators and external security keys. Users can register multiple authenticators per account, providing backup options and cross-device flexibility. Session Security Beyond FIDO2 FIDO2 authenticates users, but session management requires additional security measures. SuperTokens provides automatic token refresh, CSRF protection, and token theft detection. These session security features work regardless of authentication method, whether users authenticate via FIDO2, passwords, or social login. Hybrid Auth Flows Organizations rarely deploy a single authentication method. SuperTokens supports mixing methods: employees use FIDO2 with enterprise SSO, customers prefer social login or email OTP. The recipe system allows adding authentication methods without rewriting existing code: SuperTokens . init ( { recipeList : [ EmailPassword . init ( ) , ThirdParty . init ( { signInAndUpFeature : { providers : [ ThirdParty . Google . init ( ) ] } } ) , WebAuthn . init ( ) , Session . init ( ) ] } ) ; Future-Proof Starting with basic authentication and expanding capabilities as requirements evolve avoids over-engineering. Add email authentication initially, then introduce FIDO2 when users request stronger security. As passkey adoption increases, enable the feature by activating the WebAuthn recipe without modifying existing accounts or session management. Conclusion U2F established phishing-resistant authentication as a viable security control. FIDO2 extends these security properties while addressing U2F’s limitations: passwordless support, platform authenticators, and universal browser compatibility. The five key differences affect implementation decisions: Scope : FIDO2’s dual support for multi-factor and passwordless authentication provides deployment flexibility Standards : WebAuthn and CTAP2 separation creates clear boundaries between web APIs and device communication Devices : Platform authenticator support eliminates hardware procurement for many users Browser Support : Universal implementation versus deprecated status Passwordless : Resident credentials enable password elimination For new implementations, use FIDO2. The standard has industry backing through the passkeys initiative, comprehensive browser support, and active ecosystem development. Existing U2F deployments should plan migration before browser support ends completely. SuperTokens simplifies FIDO2 adoption by handling protocol complexity and providing session security beyond authentication. The recipe system supports gradual capability expansion, allowing organizations to start with basic authentication and add FIDO2 when requirements justify it.

title: Video Sales Funnel: Increasing Conversions with Video
summary: Learn how to structure a video sales funnel that drives conversions, track key engagement metrics, and automate follow-ups for better results.
body_text: Getting prospects to watch your videos is easy—turning that attention into real pipeline growth is the challenge. Too often, video content sits in silos, failing to guide buyers through the sales process or provide clear engagement signals for follow-up. A video sales funnel solves this by aligning different types of video with each stage of the buyer’s journey, ensuring your content attracts, nurtures, and converts leads effectively. This guide covers how to structure your funnel, track key metrics, and automate follow-ups —so you’re not just creating videos, but using them to drive revenue. What is a video sales funnel and why does it matter? A video sales funnel is a structured approach to using video content at different stages of the buyer’s journey to attract, engage, and convert prospects. Instead of relying solely on text-based marketing, it leverages video’s ability to build trust, explain complex ideas quickly, and drive action. While similar to traditional sales funnels, a video sales funnel is more dynamic—it can combine awareness-stage content, product demos, testimonials, and interactive videos to guide prospects toward a decision. Compared to static content, video is often more engaging and persuasive, helping to reduce friction and shorten sales cycles. Next, we’ll break down the key stages of a video sales funnel and how to use the right types of videos at each step. Key stages of a high-converting video sales funnel A strong video sales funnel moves buyers from first touch to conversion by delivering the right video content at the right time. Each stage has a distinct purpose, from building awareness to guiding purchase decisions. Below, we break down the key stages and the types of videos that drive results. The role of video evolves throughout the funnel, aligning with each buyer’s decision-making experience, driving them toward conversion. Awareness: Using video to reach your target audience At this stage, the goal is to attract attention and introduce your brand. Short, engaging videos—such as social media clips, explainer videos, and industry insights —help you connect with potential buyers. Distribution matters as much as content. Posting videos across social channels, paid ads, YouTube, and industry blogs ensures they reach the right audience. SEO-optimized videos can also capture search traffic, bringing in high-intent prospects early in their journey. Interest: Using webinars to capture and track buyer interest Once you have their attention, webinars and longer-form content help deepen engagement. Live and on-demand webinars provide value-driven insights, while tracking attendance and interactions helps you gauge intent. Webinars also act as lead qualifiers. Attendance, engagement levels, and post-webinar follow-ups help you identify which prospects are just exploring and which are actively evaluating solutions, allowing for more strategic outreach. Consideration: Nurturing leads with personalized, relevant video content At this stage, prospects need more context before making a decision. Case study videos, product demos , and personalized sales videos address specific pain points and objections, keeping leads engaged. Video personalization increases conversions. Sending tailored videos based on buyer activity —such as a demo that highlights features relevant to their use case—creates a more compelling experience and builds trust faster than generic content. Decision: Using video to support conversion-focused sales conversations Now, video works to reinforce buying decisions. Customer testimonials, comparison videos, and detailed product walkthroughs help build trust and handle last-minute concerns, making it easier for prospects to commit. Sales teams can leverage video at this stage. Short, one-to-one video messages from reps can answer final questions, walk through pricing, or offer a quick summary of next steps—helping to close deals faster. Building your video sales funnel: Strategies, formats, and examples for every stage Creating a video sales funnel isn’t just about matching content to each stage—it’s about supporting the entire buyer’s journey with the right formats, targeting, and follow-up strategies. While some of the elements below align directly with awareness, interest, consideration, and decision, others—like audience targeting and engagement tracking—play a foundational or supporting role in making your funnel more effective. Targeting your ideal audience with precision Before you create video content, you need to ensure it reaches the right audience. Targeting sits before and alongside the awareness stage, ensuring that your highest-value prospects engage with the content most relevant to them. Instead of broad distribution, an effective video funnel prioritizes precision —delivering videos to high-intent prospects based on industry, job title, or past interactions. For example, Reach by Banzai gives you access to a large, filterable database of verified contacts—so you can identify and target decision-makers that match your ICP. This helps ensure your awareness-stage videos are delivered to high-intent prospects, not just pushed to a broad audience. Reach by Banzai helps you identify and focus on high-intent prospects. Awareness: Short-form educational content to capture attention At this stage, your goal isn’t to sell—it’s to educate and build familiarity. Short, engaging videos introduce prospects to your brand, industry insights, or key problems they might face while positioning you as a trusted source of information. Best video formats: Social media clips (LinkedIn, YouTube Shorts, TikTok) Explainer videos (brief, high-impact overviews of key concepts) Industry trend insights (establish authority and relevance) Example: OpenReel by Banzai makes it easy to record high-quality short-form content remotely, so teams can create professional videos without needing a production crew. As engagement builds, Banzai’s Demio can host live or automated webinars that guide prospects further into the funnel. OpenReel makes it easy to record and create branded video content. Interest: Product demos and explainer videos to qualify leads Once prospects show interest, the goal is to help them self-qualify by showcasing how your product solves their problem. Videos at this stage should demonstrate value, clarify product benefits, and answer early questions. Best formats: Live or recorded product demos (walkthroughs showcasing key features) Explainer videos (break down how your solution works and why it matters) Webinars (more detailed deep dives into product capabilities) Example: Product demo videos are particularly effective at this stage, as they allow prospects to evaluate fit before speaking to sales. By embedding demo videos on high-intent pages (like pricing or feature pages), you can increase engagement and lead conversion rates. Demio’s automated product demos can include multiple engagement features including live chat and handouts. Consideration: Case studies and testimonials to nurture and build trust At this point, prospects are actively comparing solutions and looking for evidence that your product works. Video is especially useful here because it provides social proof and real-world success stories in a format that’s easier to consume than long-form case studies. Best formats: Case study videos (real-world success stories from customers) Testimonial clips (short, direct quotes from satisfied users) Before-and-after comparisons (showcasing the impact of your product) Example: Instead of a generic case study, consider a customer-led narrative, where the buyer explains their problem, what alternatives they considered, and why they chose your solution. These videos can be embedded in sales outreach, demo follow-ups, and landing pages to reinforce credibility when prospects are weighing their options. Decision: Personalized sales videos and live demos At the decision stage, buyers need reassurance, clarity, and a final push. A one-size-fits-all approach won’t work—personalized sales videos and live demos are highly effective at addressing individual concerns and closing deals. Best formats: Personalized sales outreach videos (one-to-one messages addressing specific needs) Live Q&A sessions and deep-dive demos (handling final objections in real time) Example: OpenReel makes it easy for sales teams to record customized follow-up videos that address specific objections or concerns. Meanwhile, Demio’s interactive demo software allows prospects to see the product in action, ask final questions, and gain confidence in their decision. Capturing and using video engagement data to prioritize leads Not all video views indicate buying intent— engagement data helps identify serious prospects and determine the right follow-up actions. This step sits between consideration and decision, ensuring that your sales team focuses on the leads most likely to convert. Key engagement signals: Completion rates: Who watches a video all the way through vs. drops off early? CTA clicks: Who signs up for a demo, downloads content, or requests pricing? Replay activity: Who re-watches key sections, signaling high interest? Example: With Demio, you can integrate video engagement data with your CRM , allowing you to prioritize engaged leads and tailor your outreach based on which webinar CTAs they clicked, how long they watched, and whether they interacted with polls or chat. Automating video follow-ups and retargeting to drive conversions Following up manually after every video interaction isn’t scalable. Instead, automation ensures that prospects receive the right content at the right time, based on their level of engagement. Best practices for automated video follow-ups: Trigger email sequences based on video engagement (e.g. send a deeper case study to someone who watched 75% of a demo). Retarget site visitors with relevant video ads (keep your brand top-of-mind with related content). Use chatbots or AI-driven outreach to follow up with engaged prospects instantly. Example: Syncing Demio’s video engagement data with HubSpot or Marketo helps you respond dynamically to prospect behavior. If a lead drops off midway through a webinar, they can receive an automated follow-up with a recap video or key takeaways. If they watch to the end but don’t take action, they can be sent a personalized offer or product deep dive. Measuring success: Video sales funnel metrics to track Tracking key video sales funnel metrics helps you refine strategy, improve engagement, and connect video content to real business outcomes. With the right video marketing tools, you can see where prospects drop off, track which videos drive conversions, and optimize future campaigns based on engagement data. Use the following information to see how to track the right metrics and then use this data to improve your results. Awareness and reach metrics Measure how well your videos attract new audiences. Views & impressions: Track registrants vs. attendees to see how many people actually engage with your content. Click-through rate (CTR): Use in-video CTAs to direct viewers to the next step and measure how many take action. Traffic sources: Identify which video marketing channels drive high-intent registrations by tracking referral links and UTM parameters. Demio’s Featured Actions are custom CTAs you can embed in your videos to drive prospects through the video sales funnel. Engagement and intent signals Assess whether your videos hold attention and signal buyer interest. Watch time & completion rates: Review drop-off points to identify where engagement weakens and adjust content accordingly. Poll & chat participation: Analyze interactive engagement to see which topics resonate and who’s actively engaging. CTA clicks: Identify which in-event actions drive conversions, such as resource downloads or demo sign-ups. Lead conversion rates Determine how video impacts pipeline growth. Webinar sign-ups vs. attendance: Compare registrations to actual attendance to refine follow-up strategies. Demo requests & gated content downloads: Track who takes action after watching a video, integrating data into your CRM. Pipeline influence: Connect video engagement with sales outcomes to measure impact on closed deals. Post-conversion video impact Measure how video supports retention, expansion, and advocacy. Customer onboarding completion rates: Track which onboarding videos customers complete vs. abandon to improve retention. Expansion & upsell conversions: Use engagement data from product education videos to identify upgrade opportunities. Customer advocacy: Measure how testimonial videos influence referrals and word-of-mouth growth. Demio’s People Reports allow you to segment leads, access their activity log, and measure campaign performance. Optimizing your video sales funnel for better results A well-structured video sales funnel does more than just attract views—it moves prospects through the buying journey, from awareness to conversion. By using targeted video content at each stage, tracking key engagement metrics, and automating follow-ups, you can turn video into a powerful revenue driver. The right platform makes this process easier by providing engagement insights, CRM integrations, and automation tools that help you refine strategy and prioritize high-intent leads. As you measure performance and optimize based on real data, your video sales funnel can become increasingly scalable, high-converting, and automated.

title: Battery plant hopes to put charge in New Orleans economy
summary: The company is developing a “more efficient” lithium-ion battery at an industrial park across the street from NASA’s Michoud Assembly Center.
body_text: The electronic age is creating a new industrial revolution. New Orleans East is now a player in the race to build a better rechargeable battery. Tuesday, city leaders cut the ribbon on the new Advano facility in the east. The company is developing a “more efficient” lithium-ion battery at an industrial park across the street from NASA’s Michoud Assembly Center. “This is what’s exciting because we can actually leapfrog this marketplace and lead in battery technology,” Advano CEO Chris York said. York said the process involves replacing the graphite in the core of today’s batteries produced in China with a silicon carbon composite. York claims his battery can hold a longer charge, while requiring less time to charge up. The first target is to develop the technology for electric vehicles, then expand into products such as cellphones, smartwatches, and computers. “We plan to be one of the top three players in this marketplace to advance to the next level of battery range and development,” York said. To be successful, Advano will need to take a procedure, originally developed at Tulane University, and repurpose it for creating battery materials. Mayor Latoya Cantrell called Advano, not only the next generation of rechargeable batteries, but high-tech jobs as well. “The future is right here and right here in the city of New Orleans,” Cantrell said. While Advano is a pilot program, New Orleans leaders are hoping that one day New Orleans East can become a hub for this type of advanced energy technology. “I’m just happy that we’re in New Orleans East and that we’re in New Orleans,” City Councilman Oliver Thomas said. “This is something we can be proud of.” Right now, Advano has 15 employees in New Orleans. The company would like to increase that number to 50 by the end of next year. If Advano is able to scale up its operation, CEO York said that could eventually mean up to 300 well-paying jobs for the region. BACK TO TOP

Third quarter results included net unfavorable items of $1.985 billion, $2.06 per diluted share, as follows: $1.908 billion, $1.98 per diluted share, loss on impairment of assets, net of tax; $75 million, $0.08 per diluted share, loss on conversion of debt to equity; and $2 million of other unfavorable items, net. After consideration of these net unfavorable items, third quarter 2025 adjusted net income was $62 million, $0.06 earnings per diluted share. Contract drilling revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2025, increased sequentially by $40 million to $1.03 billion, primarily due to higher revenues associated with improved rig utilization, improved revenue efficiency, an additional day in the quarter, and an increase in dayrate for one rig, partially offset by lower revenues generated by one rig that was idle between contracts. Operating and maintenance expense was $584 million, compared to $599 million in the prior quarter. The sequential decrease was primarily due to lower expenses on a rig that completed a special periodic survey during the second quarter. Interest expense was $140 million, compared with $141 million in the prior quarter, excluding the effect of the bifurcated exchange feature of the 4.625% exchangeable bonds due 2029, which represented an unfavorable adjustment of $14 million and a favorable adjustment of $29 million in the third and second quarter, respectively. Interest income was $12 million, compared to $10 million in the prior quarter. The Effective Tax Rate(2) was (1.4)%, down from 14.2% in the prior quarter. The decrease was primarily due to losses on rig impairments and changes in the internal ownership of certain rigs. Excluding discrete items, the Effective Tax Rate was 34.8% compared to 70.0% in the previous quarter. In the third quarter, cash paid for taxes was $11 million. Cash provided by operating activities was $246 million during the third quarter, representing an increase of $118 million compared to the prior quarter. The sequential increase was primarily due to a reduction of working capital. Third quarter 2025 capital expenditures were $11 million, compared to $24 million in the prior quarter. “In addition to delivering an outstanding quarter of operational performance and Free Cash Flow generation, we took decisive steps to accelerate debt reduction and improve our financial flexibility,” said President and Chief Executive Officer, Keelan Adamson. “Along with meeting scheduled maturities, these transactions are expected to, respectively, reduce total debt by approximately $1.2 billion by the end of 2025; annual interest expense by approximately $83 million; and restricted cash by $52 million.” Adamson concluded, “As a result, we have also significantly improved our debt maturity profile over the next several years and believe these actions will further enhance shareholder value.” Non-GAAP Financial Measures We present our operating results in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S. (“U.S. GAAP”). We believe certain financial measures, such as EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Net Income and Free Cash Flow, which are non-GAAP measures, provide users of our financial statements with supplemental information that may be useful in evaluating our operating performance. About Transocean Transocean is a leading international provider of offshore contract drilling services for oil and gas wells. The company specializes in technically demanding sectors of the global offshore drilling business with a particular focus on ultra-deepwater and harsh environment drilling services, and operates the highest specification floating offshore drilling fleet in the world. Transocean owns or has partial ownership interests in and operates a fleet of 27 mobile offshore drilling units, consisting of 20 ultra-deepwater floaters and seven harsh environment floaters. For more information about Transocean, please visit: www.deepwater.com .
